title: The perfect cutting chai, village style ☕️🔥 #shorts
dish_fact: The Indian habit of 'pulling' chai - pouring it in a long stream between two pots - isn't a trick: it cools and aerates the tea, blending the milk and spices into that signature frothy top.

segments.moment_description: Misty village morning: the young woman snaps a thumb of fresh ginger and pinches a few tulsi leaves from a clay pot in her little garden, dew dripping, soft blue morning light, Studio Ghibli style

Water comes to a rolling boil in a small blackened brass pot over a glowing clay wood stove; a stone crushes the ginger on a board and green cardamom pods, cloves and a few peppercorns are cracked and dropped in, the water tinting and fragrant steam curling up, close-up
A spoon of loose black tea and a spoon of sugar are stirred into the bubbling spiced water; it darkens to a deep amber and rises in a rolling, foamy boil, close macro of the churning surface

A steady stream of fresh milk is poured from a steel tumbler into the dark tea; it blooms pale then surges up into a big creamy froth threatening to boil over as she lifts the pot, warm firelight glow
The chai is 'pulled': lifted high and poured in a long thin frothy ribbon from one pot down into another held low, back and forth, aerating it, steam trailing the stream against the dark kitchen

The finished chai poured through a small strainer into a rustic clay kulhad until a creamy froth caps the rim, steam rising, a couple of rusk biscuits resting on the saucer beside it - the cozy reveal

description:
Masala Chai — made the traditional North Indian village way. 🌿
The Indian habit of 'pulling' chai - pouring it in a long stream between two pots - isn't a trick: it cools and aerates the tea, blending the milk and spices into that signature frothy top.
Made with water, milk, black tea leaves, ginger, green cardamom, cloves and love.
